Glacier to share top-6 enterprise target list and associated champions (Olivia)
Ethan to run quick perf sketch on 50k token long-context workflow and share latency/cost numbers (Ethan)

summary: Weekly channel-alliance session to map Glacier's pipeline to Redwood co-sell motions. Focus was on identifying top priority deals, surface technical risk areas (long-context throughput, VPC/private model requirements), and align on next steps for an exec-level handoff. Agreement to share account list and run targeted perf sketches; Redwood to provide co-sell economics and partner playbook draft.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Samira P., Ethan M., Jordan B. (Redwood) — Olivia C., Raj M., Maya F., Tom A. (Glacier)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call and then we can jump in. We wanted to map deals and call out risk so we can prioritize co-sell motions.
[00:15] Olivia: Thanks Samira, hi all. We have a handful of north-amer enterprise deals where we think Redwood could be a good fit, and we wanted to align on who from your side will own the technical checks.
[00:30] Jordan: Hi — Jordan here, partnerships. I can own the commercial mapping, Sen? (laugh) — Samira will own demos and AE flow, and Ethan's our SE for deeper perf work.
[00:45] Ethan: Hey, good to meet folks. Tom, I understand you run the field CTO org?
[00:50] Tom: Yeah, I'm the field CTO, focused on platform integrations. We have one account specifically pushing for private deployment with KMS integration.
[00:58] Raj: And we have an active RFP where the customer insists on SOC2 plus on-prem options — that's a key gating factor.
[01:10] Samira: Got it. To structure this, I sketched three buckets: quick-win deals (hosted API ok), mid-term (dedicated or VPC), and long-term strategic where on-prem or deeper ISV integrations are required. We'll walk each account into those buckets.
[01:25] Maya: Sounds good. I'll pull up the spreadsheet — apologies, coming in on mobile for a sec.
[01:33] [01:33] Maya (phone): ok, um I have the list --- top 8 accounts, note: two are in healthcare and need data residency controls.
[01:45] Ethan: Healthcare usually pushes private or dedicated with strict logs, encryption, HSM/KMS — we should flag those. Our Private offering supports customer-managed KMS, and we can surface audit log retention.
[01:58] Olivia: On economics, we need to understand partner rebates / crediting so we can pitch co-sell. Jordan, do we have a sample structure?
[02:10] Jordan: We do — baseline is a referral fee plus a back-end revenue share on committed reserved capacity. We'll send a one-pager after the call. Exact splits depend on ARR thresholds.
[02:25] Raj: Also want to make sure the sales motion is clear — who will own the primary relationship post-close? Glacier typically wants to keep the account ownership.
[02:35] Samira: That's standard, Glacier would be primary, Redwood to provide customer success for onboarding and in-product support; we can also co-sell on annual renewals when we're materially driving usage. We should codify that in the playbook.
[02:50] [03:00] (small cross talk)
[03:15] Samira: Ok let's start mapping accounts — Maya, can you walk us through the top 6?
[03:23] Maya: Sure. Account A — financial services, has production PII, requires SOC2 and SSO, timeline Q4 close. Account B — mid-market retail, open to hosted. Account C — large healthcare provider, timeline Q1 next year, must be private. Account D — managed service provider who've asked for embedding roadmap and white label. Account E, F are smaller pilots.
[03:55] Ethan: For Account A (finserv), latency and SLAs are important. Would you expect sub-200ms token latencies or is throughput more important?
[04:05] Raj: I think for that use case they care more about consistent latency — the underwriting flow is user-facing.
[04:12] Ethan: Ok, we can propose Dedicated with configured autoscale and latency SLOs. Need to surface typical tails and think about warm KV cache if there are repetitive prompts.
[04:24] Tom: Quick Q — does Redwood do prefix caching across sessions or just per-request?
[04:30] Ethan: We have prefix/KV caching and we can pin certain prompt completions into a warm cache for the session type; I'll include more details in the perf sketch.
[04:40] Olivia: For Account C (healthcare, private), I want to make sure we don't underestimate the security review timeline — typically 8–12 weeks.
[04:48] Samira: Noted. We'll treat that as long lead. For the mid-market retail open to hosted, that's your easiest entry point.
[04:56] [05:10] Jordan: Quick commercial note — when Glacier is primary and introduces an account, we usually provide 6 months of partner rebate if the deal hits certain thresholds — again we'll document.
[05:22] Raj: We also have one tricky deal — the customer wants on-prem integration into an air-gapped environment. How do you handle that?
[05:31] Ethan: We have an on-prem package, but the recent builds require some engineering runway; shipping to air-gapped environments can be more of an engineering engagement and may need a pilot statement of work. We'll surface constraints and rough lead times.
[05:45] Maya: Account D is specifically pushing for white-label; they want to bundle our combined offering and resell as part of their managed platform.
[05:53] Samira: That can be a strategic ISV motion. We'll flag it as go-to-market require pricing and an OEM-ish contract. Jordan, can you handle the initial T&Cs?
[06:02] Jordan: Yes, I'll draft a starter term sheet for OEM/resell and send.
[06:08] [06:20] (brief pause while Jordan types)
[06:36] Olivia: Another question — for co-sell attribution, how will bookings be recognized in your CRM? We need clear measurables for commission.
[06:47] Samira: We can set up a partner-led opportunity stage and a field to flag Glacier as introducing partner. We'll coordinate with support to patch CRM mappings; that's in our standard partner enablement kit.
[07:00] Raj: Technical triage — we have two main risk buckets: long-context throughput (50k tokens for docs) and VPC/private deployment + KMS. Which is the higher risk?
[07:12] Ethan: Long-context is tricky. In practice performance/cost varies a lot by model and quantization; we can run a focused sketch on a representative OCR->embedding->QA pipeline. That will give us rough latency and cost numbers to share.
[07:26] Tom: The OCR pipeline does chunking, but they want end-to-end <= 2s per query for certain flows and can tolerate higher for batch indexing.
[07:36] Ethan: 2s is ambitious for 50k context unless heavy caching or retrieval augmentation is used. We'll scope options: (a) aggressive prefix caching + retrieval, (b) chunked post-processing, (c) specialized long-context variants. I'll model all three.
[07:49] Olivia: If you could share a simple table of latency/cost per 1k tokens for each option that'd be super helpful to position vs competitors.
[07:57] Samira: We'll do that. Also, we should call out competitor differentiation — for example Anthropic and OpenAI have different SLAs and pricing but Redwood can support private deployments which is a plus.
[08:10] [08:30] Maya: small note — Account A wants a proof-of-concept next month. Can Redwood commit to a 2-week POC with a hosted sandbox?
[08:38] Samira: Yes for hosted we can do a 2-week POC; for private it'd be longer. We should confirm data residency and if they need any PII redaction.
[08:48] Raj: Also need SSO/SAML for the POC.
[08:52] Ethan: SAML can be set up for hosted POCs; I'll send the steps.
[09:00] Jordan: Commercial ask — is there a standard starter discount for partner-originated POCs?
[09:07] Samira: We usually offer credits and joint-marketing support. Details in the one-pager.
[09:15] [09:30] Olivia: Let's walk deal-by-deal quickly. Account A — finance (Q4) — suggested Redwood motion: Dedicated SLOs, demo week this month, POC next month. Primary risk: SAML and audit log detail.
[09:45] Samira: Agreed. Ethan will own the SAML checklist and perf sketch; Jordan will craft the commercial template.
[09:52] [10:10] (background phone ringing for a sec)
[10:22] Maya: Account B — retail — they prefer hosted. Could be a quick win.
[10:28] Samira: Hosted is fastest to close. We can offer an optimized plan to keep token cost down — Redwood Optimize suggestions: batching and caching.
[10:37] Ethan: For retail, typical pattern: lower per-request latency needed but tolerance for variability. We'll propose a small trial with caching enabled.
[10:45] Raj: Account C — healthcare private — long lead. We'll need SOC2 evidence and data residency for EU clients.
[10:53] Samira: We'll send our SOC2 snapshot and controls mapping; Redwood can point to Private with customer-managed keys.
[11:00] Tom: For private, what's the typical install time?
[11:04] Ethan: Depends—simple VPC deployment can be done in weeks with customer infra ready; fully air-gapped on-prem could be months. We'll provide estimates in the follow-up.
[11:15] Olivia: One more meta-question: will Redwood co-brand materials or expect Glacier to lead with its own branding?
[11:22] Jordan: Co-branding typically allowed in joint marketing collateral; we can do a co-sell deck with both logos.
[11:30] [11:45] Samira: Ok technical deep dive planning: Ethan, can you run two sketches — one for 50k token OCR flow and one for a 5k token high-frequency low-latency flow — and return a doc with cost/latency tradeoffs?
[11:58] Ethan: Yes. I'll include headroom sizing for Dedicated nodes and estimated burst costs. Also will note quantization impacts.
[12:07] Raj: Please be explicit about model variants used in the sketch — if it's a custom large model vs a smaller open model, costs differ.
[12:15] Ethan: Will do; I'll run experiments on the top candidate models and include an appendix.
[12:22] Maya: For Account D OEM ask — they'll want SSO and reseller pricing as well as a revenue share.
[12:30] Samira: We'll include OEM pricing examples in the playbook. Jordan to draft.
[12:38] [12:45] Olivia: Security reviewers will ask about audit trails, KMS, and where logs are stored. Do you have a publicly scannable security checklist we can share?
[12:55] Samira: Yes — we'll share a link to Redwood security pack and SOC2 mapping. Note: some of the field names in our docs might be abbreviated, so please ping if anything is missing.
[13:05] Tom: Also ask about data retention windows — the customer wants 30-day minimal retention by default and options to purge.
[13:12] Ethan: Our retention policies can be configured; for Private installations the customer controls retention. For hosted we have configurable TTLs.
[13:20] Raj: On risk triage, can we classify each account as green/amber/red for GTM and tech?
[13:27] Samira: Let's do that quickly. Account A - amber (comms/SSO risk), Account B - green (hosted ok), Account C - red (private + data residency), Account D - amber (OEM contract negotiation), E/F - green (pilots).
[13:45] Maya: I'll record that.
[13:50] [14:10] Jordan: Commercial nuance — for deals with reserved capacity we can offer committed discounts; Glacier may have to agree to signal volume. We'll show example tiers.
[14:22] Olivia: For the customer's procurement folks, we may need a term sheet and security attestation before demo. Can Redwood provide an NDA + standard term sheet?
[14:32] Samira: Yes — we'll send NDA and a standard SOW template.
[14:40] Ethan: Technical note — if a customer wants encryption-in-use via HSM, we can integrate with common KMS/HSM providers but that'll add complexity. We'll call it out in the SOW.
[14:52] Raj: How do you handle multi-region concerns? Some accounts want EU-only processing.
[14:59] Ethan: We can pin model instances to specific regions in Redwood Private or Dedicated; hosted also offers region pinning for enterprise tiers. We'll include region options in the follow-up.
[15:10] [15:30] Olivia: Anything else on commercial?
[15:35] Jordan: Just to confirm, Glacier wants partner rebates for the first 6-12 months for partner-originated deals. We'll bake that into the one-pager.
[15:45] Samira: Agreed.
[15:52] [16:10] (brief silence as people type)
[16:33] Ethan: Quick clarification — for the perf sketch, do you have representative documents we can run on? PDFs with OCR would be ideal.
[16:43] Olivia: Yes, we can share redacted samples. I'll get those over in the next couple days.
[16:50] Tom: We also need to decide on demo ownership — Glacier will do initial demo with customer then Redwood SE to join for deep technical Q&A.
[16:59] Samira: That works. We'll plan a joint demo: Glacier-led with Redwood SE on the tail.
[17:05] Raj: Timeline check — customer A expects a demo in late September. Can we commit to a slot week of 9/22?
[17:13] Samira: We can — Samira tentatively assigns Ethan and Jordan to that week, pending calendar confirmation.
[17:20] Maya: noted.
[17:25] [17:45] Olivia: On legal, any red flags in the standard SOW for OEM/resell?
[17:53] Jordan: No show stoppers but OEM requires explicit IP terms and reseller liability carve-outs — I'll highlight those in the term sheet.
[18:05] Samira: Ok we're approaching the end — let's recap: Redwood to send co-sell playbook, security pack, and perf sketch. Glacier to send account list and sample docs. Schedule exec sync on 9/24.
[18:20] Raj: Confirmed.
[18:25] Samira: Anything else from anyone?
[18:28] (slight pause)
[18:32] Maya: No, thanks everyone.
[18:35] Olivia: Thanks — talk soon.
[18:38] Samira: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[END] Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlaps at times; auto-captions mis-typed a few product names.

Attachments referenced during call:
- Partner deck: https://redwood-demo.s3/partner-deck-channel-alliance-v2.pdf
- Glacier accounts (shared): https://glacier.share/enterprise-targets.xlsx
- Security pack link (to be sent): Redwood security checklist (SOC2 mapping)

Recap (verbatim from meeting close):
Samira: "We'll send co-sell one-pager, security pack and run perf sketches — Glacier will send prioritized accounts and redacted doc samples. Plan exec sync 9/24."
